Interactive showcase

Everything Valentine does, in one place

A read-only agent for venture funds. Give it a founder or a company and, before you walk into the call, it tells you whether anyone at your fund has already talked to them — who, when, and what happened.

One verdict

Not a search result — a single line a partner reads in two seconds and acts on.

Read-only

No write tools exist in the codebase. It looks, it never touches.

Your keys

Runs locally with your own CRM + model keys. Nothing leaves the fund.

The problem it closes

It's 9:58am, the call is at 10:00. The note exists, the email is in someone's inbox — but you walk in blind, about to re-pitch a deal a partner already passed on, or double-track a company someone owns. Valentine closes that two-minute gap.

Live demo · simulated

Watch a sweep

Pick a target. Valentine runs the same loop it runs for real — search_crm → get_context → submit_verdict — against sample data. No keys, nothing real touched.

~/fund — valentine
$ valentine acme.com

Machine-readable verdict — exit code encodes the outcome:

Exit codes: 0 clean · 10 prior contact · 20 ambiguous · 1 error — so watch, Slack, and scripts can branch on the result.

The heart of the product

Every run resolves to one of three

A verdict always carries who (owner), when (last touch), what happened (status), and the record IDs it used. Never a 40-row dump.

⚠
Prior contact — a matching record has an owner + history. The important case: when in doubt, Valentine chooses this.⚠ Sarah owns Acme — emailed founder May 11, logged "passed, too early."
✅
Clean — no matching record, or a record with no interactions, lists, notes, or owner. A valid answer, not an error.✅ No prior contact on record.
❓
Ambiguous — multiple weak matches it can't confidently disambiguate.❓ 2 possible matches — "Acme Inc" (Sarah) and "Acme Labs" (unowned).

The signals it weighs

Interactions

lastEmail, lastMeeting, lastInteraction, firstInteraction, and connectionStrength.

Ownership

The relationship owner — the partner who "has" the company.

List memberships

A "Passed", "Portfolio", or pipeline list + deal stage (e.g. "In DD").

Notes & people

Outcomes like "passed, too early", plus linked people already in the CRM.

Three moving parts

Small enough to read every line

~300 lines total. Click a part to see what it does. Design rule: the agent and triggers never import a specific CRM — only the CRMConnector interface.

🎯 Trigger
how a sweep starts
src/cli.ts · watch.ts
→
🧠 Agent
the ~40-line loop
src/agent.ts · prompt.ts
→
🔌 Connector
read-only CRM access
src/connectors/*
Trigger — how a sweep gets kicked off. The CLI (valentine acme.com), the MCP server, and the /valentine Slack command (valentine slack) today; watch (calendar) on the roadmap. Triggers depend only on the connector interface, never a specific CRM.
Agent — the loop, hand-rolled on a minimal Messages surface (Anthropic API or local Ollama via a small adapter): model thinks → calls a read tool → gets the result → repeats → calls submit_verdict exactly once. Model- and provider-swappable. Its operating rules live in src/prompt.ts — read-only, always. Tools available: search_crm, get_context, submit_verdict.
Connector — implements a tiny interface: whoami(), search(), getContext(). Attio, Affinity, and Salesforce ship today; HubSpot is one new file away. Crucially, the interface exposes no mutating methods — read-only is enforced by absence, not config.

Connectors

Attio shipped

First-class. Companies + people search, interaction signals, notes, lists.

Affinity shipped

Interaction dates, list membership, notes. No org-level owner exposed by their v1.

Salesforce shipped

Standard objects via SOQL: Accounts, Contacts, notes, tasks, opportunities.

HubSpot one file away

Implement the interface — zero changes elsewhere. Write your own in an afternoon.

Models & providers

Model

claude-haiku-4-5 (default, near-zero cost) · claude-sonnet-4-6 (sharper, ~10×) · any tool-calling Ollama model (free, local).

Provider

Anthropic API & local / Ollama today. AWS Bedrock listed, disabled until wired.

A sweep is a few short tool round-trips + a one-line answer — roughly a cent or two on Sonnet, near-zero on Haiku. Target: p50 < 8s, ≤ 6 tool calls.

Load-bearing for trust

It reads. It never writes.

This is a tool you point at a live CRM on day one — reading every founder you've ever passed on. The guarantees are structural, not promises.

🔒 Read-only, structurally

No write tools exist in the codebase. The connector interface exposes no mutating methods. Enforced by absence.

🤐 Never sends, never moves

No messaging, no deal-stage changes, no emails.

💻 Local & BYO-key

Keys live on your machine. Data flows only between your CRM and your chosen model. No Valentine servers.

🔗 Cited

Every verdict references the record IDs it used.

👁 Auditable

~300 lines. A fund's eng can read all of it before trusting it.

⚖️ MIT

Clone it, read every line, fork it. No black box between you and your founders.

💡 Nine directions Valentine could go

These go beyond the shipped roadmap — raw ideas to spark yours. Each keeps the read-only, one-verdict, local-first soul. Click to expand.

1Warm-intro pathfinder networkNot just "have we talked" — "who's our warmest way in?"›

When a company is clean, the follow-up question is always "so how do I reach them?" Valentine already reads linked people and connection strength. It could surface the strongest existing relationship path — "Daniel is 1st-degree with their VP Eng; connection Very strong" — turning a dead end into a next step.

Stays read-only. Pairs naturally with a network/graph connector. Verdict gains an optional intro_path field.

2Conflict & double-track radar teamFlag when two partners are quietly tracking the same deal.›

A batch/daily mode that sweeps the active pipeline and emits a short digest of overlaps: two owners on adjacent records, a portfolio company competing with a new inbound, a founder you passed on now re-entering. The "make a fund look like it talks to itself" use case, run proactively instead of on demand.

New trigger (cron/watch), same verdict engine, aggregated. Output: a ranked list of collisions with owners + citations.

3Verdict history & diff memory"Since you last checked Acme, Sarah logged a meeting."›

Locally cache each verdict (already provenance-friendly — config lives in ~/.valentine/). On re-run, show what changed: a new note, a stage move, a fresh interaction. Turns Valentine from a point-in-time check into a lightweight watch on the companies you care about — without polling the CRM constantly.

Local-only store, still read-only against the CRM. Great input for watch notifications.

4Batch sweep from a calendar file / list workflowvalentine --batch today.ics → verdicts for every attendee.›

Point it at an .ics, a CSV of domains, or a pasted list of attendees and get one verdict per target, sorted so the ⚠ prior-contacts float to the top. The "prep for the whole day in one command" mode — a stepping stone to full watch that needs no calendar integration.

Reuses the CLI + --json. Bounded fan-out, respects the ≤6-tool-calls-per-sweep budget per target.

5Confidence score on the verdict qualityHow sure is it? Surface it, don't hide it.›

Attach a calibrated confidence (high / medium / low) derived from match quality and signal count. A high-confidence ⚠ reads differently from a shaky one — and it makes ambiguous less of a cliff. Scriptable too: only alert on high-confidence prior-contacts in watch.

One new optional field on Verdict. Rendered as a subtle tag, never louder than the summary line.

6LinkedIn / domain resolver front-door inputPaste anything — it figures out who you mean first.›

A pre-step that normalizes messy input (a person's name, a LinkedIn slug, a company alias, an email) into the right CRM query before the sweep. Reduces ambiguous verdicts caused by bad input rather than genuinely weak matches.

Pure read/resolve. Keeps external enrichment out of scope — only disambiguates, never enriches.

7"Explain this verdict" mode trustvalentine --why acme.com shows the reasoning trail.›

For the skeptical partner: an optional verbose mode that prints the exact tool calls, the records examined, and which signals tipped the verdict — collapsed by default, expandable. Reinforces the auditability guarantee at the point of doubt, not just in the source.

The loop already has this data; it's a rendering mode. Off by default to keep the one-line soul intact.

8Notification channels for watch reachmacOS notification · Slack DM · email — you pick.›

An open question in the spec becomes a small pluggable notifier interface (mirroring the connector pattern): notify(verdict) with macOS, Slack DM, and email implementations. Adding a channel = one file, same as adding a CRM.

Directly unblocks P1 watch. Read-only stays intact — notifiers send heads-ups about verdicts, never touch the CRM.

9Multi-CRM merge scaleSome funds run Attio + a legacy Salesforce. Sweep both.›

A composite connector that fans a query across several configured CRMs and merges the matches before the agent weighs them. One verdict, drawn from everywhere the fund's memory actually lives. The connector interface already makes this a wrapper, not a rewrite.

Implements CRMConnector by delegating to N children. Citations gain a source tag so you know which CRM each record came from.
